code_paper_alignment.methodology_describ.reason: The Methodology matches the submitted code in most checked respects. TopoAnsatz subclasses the authors' ansatz and overrides only add_ops_dyn, inheriting one_step, get_minv and the adaptive dt. The admission rule (val_max_a ≥ val_max − τ, taansatz.py:266-267) matches Eq. (rule). Migration searches all shortest paths and splits, maximizes the locality score, and breaks ties lexicographically (taansatz.py:116-155), matching §3.3. The ablation switches, CNOT/depth conventions, pools, Hamiltonians, initial states, exact references and integrator constants all match the code and logs. Topology A TA runs reproduce the unconstrained runs exactly, as claimed. I found two inaccuracies. (1) report.tex:374-376 says the loop continues until L²<L²_cut 'exactly as in the original', and :382-385 claims the admitted quality is 'never below the growth loop's own convergence criterion'. The break test instead uses dist = hvar − val_max of the global leader (taansatz.py:258, 337), even when a different admissible operator was admitted. Logs confirm that growth events can end with the admitted L² above the cut. In ta_tau1e-4/lsm_hz-0.7_topoB/growth_log.json these values are about 1.021e-3, 1.062e-3 and 1.055e-3, and in mfim_hz0.5_topoB about 1.090e-3. records.json dist arrays contain values ≥1e-3 only in these TA runs, never in the unconstrained, naive or τ=0 runs. (2) τ→∞ is described as 'never migrate' (report.tex:421-422, 665-666), but the code falls back to migration when no admissible candidate improves. ablation_restrict/lsm_hz1.6_topoB/run.log:724 shows one 1-SWAP migration before that run aborts. Both deviations are bounded and small: the excess is ≤τ=1e-4 (≤10% of L²_cut) at a few events, and one SWAP occurs in a run that fails anyway. Neither changes the method's structure or any reported result, since fidelities are measured exactly and remain ≥0.9992. I judge these to be inaccuracies rather than a material contradiction and flag them for audit.

code_paper_alignment.topology_aware_logi.reason: The topology-aware logic in taansatz.py implements what §3 describes. It keeps a persistent logical-to-physical map π, treats one-qubit operators as always admissible, and runs an admissible leader alongside the global leader in a single pool scan. It applies the τ-tolerance rule, then a minimal (d−1)-SWAP migration over all shortest paths and splits that maximizes pool-pair locality with a lexicographic tie-break. persistent=False reverts SWAPs; locality_tiebreak=False takes the first path with m=0. The physical circuit is reconstructed for counting and audits while the statevector is evolved logically. Audit logs show 0 edge-set violations on Topologies A, B and C. Embeddings come from the stated 8! brute force (topology.py:134-152), and n_migrations=0 on Topology A as claimed. The same two bounded inaccuracies noted for the previous node apply here. First, termination is checked on the global leader's distance rather than the admitted operator's (taansatz.py:258, 337), so the claimed 'never below the convergence criterion' guarantee (report.tex:382-385) can be exceeded by ≤τ. Logged events reach admitted L²≈1.02–1.09e-3. Second, the τ=1e9 restriction limit can fall back to a migration (one 1-SWAP migration logged), contrary to 'never migrate'. These do not alter the described admission/migration structure, the topology compliance, or the reported overheads in any material way. No material contradiction was established; the issues are flagged for audit.

variational_simulation_integrity.ansatz_.reason: Ansatz-growth decisions in TopoAnsatz.add_ops_dyn use only McLachlan quantities. These are the projected distance removal dist_p from M and V, pthmax, the energy variance hvar, plus topology adjacency and the locality score. Exact states never enter the ansatz object. They are used only in runner.record_state to log fidelity, Loschmidt echo and observables after each step. growth_log.json records dist_p_global, dist_p_admissible and hvar for every admission, which shows the McLachlan-based decisions. τ selection uses final fidelity only as a pass/fail accuracy floor, which all completing τ values passed. Selection among them was by CNOT multiplier, a global hyperparameter choice rather than per-step growth driven by an oracle. Exact-state fidelity serves as independent validation only.
evidence: proposal/code/tavqds/runner.py:141-161 record_state computes fidelity after the step; exact_state not passed to ansatz

no_replication_of_published_method.not_a.reason: The contribution is a τ-tolerant, locality-constrained admission rule inside the AVQDS growth loop, combined with persistent minimal-SWAP migration targeted by a pool-locality score. The paper positions it explicitly against post-hoc routers (SABRE, t|ket⟩, A*, temporal planning, SAT/Steiner) and against hardware-efficient and hardware-aware ADAPT-VQE (Tepaske et al. 2023) and fixed ansätze. It acknowledges that the persistent-permutation idea echoes prior permutation tracking (Ito; Siraichi) and LNN compilation (Maslov), and that SWAP networks are familiar from QAOA (report.tex:201-218). The naive baseline is plainly labeled as standard insert-and-revert routing. I found no identifiable prior method that is substantively reproduced while being presented as new without acknowledgment. Literature could not be browsed in this environment; the rubric requires affirmative evidence, and none was found.
evidence: report.tex bibliography: li2019sabre, sivarajah2021, cowtan2020, siraichi2018, ito2019, maslov2017, tepaske2023, zhang2021

selective_reporting.embedding_choices_do.reason: Each (benchmark × topology) uses one embedding chosen by a deterministic, stated rule. The rule maximizes the number of local pool pairs, then minimizes the residual distance sum, then breaks ties lexicographically, over all 8! placements (topology.py:134-152). The choices and their justifications are logged in logs/embeddings/embeddings.md and embeddings.json. The same embedding appears in the summary.json of both the naive and TA runs: identity on B, [0,1,2,3,7,6,5,4] on A, identity on C. No run in the logs uses any other embedding, and nothing suggests that alternatives were tried and discarded, or that an unfavorable naive embedding was picked.
